What we're here to do

  • Introduce children to the rich tradition of Carnatic music.
  • Build a youth-led, sustainable leadership model.
  • Encourage discipline, focus, and self-expression.

Seven chapters, one club

The club is district-wide, and each school runs its own chapter, with classes after school at elementary schools across the Northshore School District. The club is still growing — new chapters opened at Lockwood, Moorlands, and Ruby Bridges this year.

Curriculum & structure

Students follow an 11-week program, building from first swaras to a live showcase for families and peers.

Level 1: Foundations

Where every student begins: the building blocks of Carnatic music.

  • Theory and basic exercises: Core Sarali swara beginner sequences.
  • Vocal technique: Warmups and pitch accuracy.
  • Showcase: Live performance for families and peers.

Level 2: Intermediate New

Introduced in 2026–27 for students who have completed Level 1, or who have basic Carnatic training from outside the club. Level 2 started this year at Canyon Creek Elementary, taught by Satvik Tadiparti.

  • Janta Swaras: Double-note patterns that build on Level 1 foundations.
  • Showcase: Live performance for families and peers.

How it runs: each chapter meets after school during the 11-week session, taught by a trained youth instructor using the club's shared curriculum, practice recordings, and structured learning materials.

Our journey and mission

In 2022, Shreya Battula envisioned a way to share her love for Carnatic music with the younger generation. What began as a small after-school club at Canyon Creek Elementary has grown to inspire 120+ students through a district-wide initiative spanning chapters at seven elementary schools.

Shreya personally trains and mentors the club's youth instructors, building a youth-led teaching model that sustains the program across all seven chapters. Every class is taught by a trained young instructor, and every instructor is coached by her.

The club is dedicated to making Indian classical music accessible, fostering musical skills alongside confidence and cultural pride.

Where we started

The club began in 2022 with five students and one instructor at Canyon Creek Elementary. Milestone by milestone — a second year, district expansion approval, and new chapters at Fernwood, Maywood Hills, and Kokanee — it has grown into a district-wide program.

New in 2026–27: the club introduced Level 2 intermediate training for returning students — Level 2 started this year at Canyon Creek Elementary, taught by Satvik Tadiparti — and three new chapters opened this year — Lockwood, Moorlands, and Ruby Bridges Elementary — bringing the club to seven chapters and 120+ students.
